{{Short description|Primary mathematics education structure in England}}
{{no footnotes|date=August 2011}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=December 2021}}

The '''National Numeracy Strategy''' was designed to facilitate a sound grounding in maths for all primary school pupils. It arose out of the National Numeracy Project in 1996, led by a [[Numeracy]] Task Force in England, and was launched in 1998 and implemented in schools in 1999. <ref>{{Cite web |title=National Numeracy Strategy |url=https://www.oxfordreference.com/display/10.1093/oi/authority.20110803100224411 |access-date=2024-03-12 |website=Oxford Reference |language=en }}</ref> The strategy included an outline of expected teaching in mathematics for all pupils from Reception to Year 6.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title={{!}} STEM |url=https://www.stem.org.uk/resources/collection/3428/national-strategies-primary-mathematics#:~:text=In%202003,%20the%20National%20Numeracy,the%20broader%20Primary%20National%20Strategy. |access-date=2024-03-12 |website=www.stem.org.uk}}</ref>

In 2003, the strategy, including the framework for teaching, was absorbed into the broader [[Primary National Strategy]]. The framework for teaching was then updated in 2006, but ceased to operate in 2011.<ref name=":0" />
